title: Embedded Frame
description: Generic frame-rendering primitive a business can attach to a message to request that the platform render a business-supplied URL. The frame's contents are opaque to the platform: it loads the URL, optionally surfaces it to the buyer, and waits for an in-frame completion signal before resubmitting on the same path. Covers non-blocking background data collection (display: hidden) and blocking buyer-interactive flows (display: visible). Use cases include 3DS device data collection, 3DS challenge, captcha and bot-detection challenges, redirect-based alternative payment method approval, and any future step-up flow that can be expressed as a hosted URL with a completion signal.

id.description: Opaque business-supplied identifier the platform echoes back on resubmission. Lets a business correlate the frame completion with a specific request when multiple frames are in flight (e.g., DDC on several payment instruments).

url.description: Absolute HTTPS URL the platform loads in the frame. Hosted by the business or a party it delegates to (e.g., its PSP). The platform does not interpret the contents; protocol-specific payloads (3DS, captcha vendors, etc.) stay between the business and its provider.

display.description: Rendering mode. 'hidden' means the platform loads the URL without exposing it to the buyer (background data collection); the platform MUST still allow the frame to execute network requests and post completion. 'visible' means the platform renders the frame to the buyer for interaction; the platform MUST surface it in a way appropriate to its UX (modal, sheet, dedicated view) and MUST allow the buyer to dismiss it.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp after which the frame is no longer valid. Platforms SHOULD stop waiting for completion past this time and resubmit reporting timeout, or surface a failure to the buyer for visible frames.

dimensions.description: Optional rendering hints for visible frames. Ignored when display is 'hidden'. Platforms MAY adapt these to their UX (e.g., a chat surface may show the frame inline at a different size).
